# Aim

Assemble the per-gene table used by the gene-level heterogeneity model: the
**label** (confident somatic-utility positive / negative / grey zone) plus the
**non-network features**. The network-proximity
feature is *not* built here — it is fold-aware and is computed inside
`Gene_utility_model.Rmd`.

Scope: **all monoallelic (dominant) DDG2P genes** are scored, but the model is
only *trained* on the subset that is **benchmarking-eligible** (>=10 unique
pathogenic AND >=10 unique benign ClinVar variants) and confidently classified
(see labels below). Utility is defined on **COSMIC** codon-count AUC
(sperm/buccal too sparse per gene). None of the model's features require
ClinVar variant counts to compute (they come from DDG2P, COSMIC CGC, gnomAD,
cancerhotspots, and STRING), so genes with too few (or zero) ClinVar variants
to benchmark individually can still be scored by the fitted model -- this is
the "grey zone" and is deliberately NOT restricted to the benchmarking-eligible
set, so the model's predictions extend to genes we cannot yet benchmark at all.

Labels (ClinVar count-weighted, `n_COSMIC_codon_count`), among benchmarking-eligible genes only:
- **positive** = AUC lower CI > 0.70
- **negative** = AUC upper CI < 0.60 AND >=15 unique pathogenic
- **grey**     = every other monoallelic DDG2P gene, whether benchmarking-eligible
  or not (scored, not trained on)

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
theme_set(theme_bw(12))

# ---- input file path and column names (edit if the source file differs) ----
# gnomAD v4.1 gene constraint metrics tsv (public: gnomad.broadinstitute.org).
# Expected columns used below: gene, mane_select, lof.oe_ci.upper (=LOEUF),
# mis.oe (=MOEUF), mis.exp (=expected missense). Adjust names here if the file
# differs.
GNOMAD_CONSTRAINT_FILE <- "../../../Data/Gnomad/gnomad.v4.1.constraint_metrics.tsv"
# COL_* below just record which column in GNOMAD_CONSTRAINT_FILE holds which
# piece of information, so the rest of the script can refer to e.g. COL_LOEUF
# rather than a hard-coded column name -- if gnomAD ever renames a column, or
# a differently-formatted file is used, only these four lines need editing
# rather than hunting through the rest of the script.
COL_GENE   <- "gene"             # gene symbol column
COL_MANE   <- "mane_select"      # TRUE/FALSE: is this row the MANE-select transcript for the gene?
COL_LOEUF  <- "lof.oe_ci.upper"  # LOEUF = loss-of-function observed/expected upper bound (constraint metric)
COL_MOEUF  <- "mis.oe"           # missense observed/expected ratio (constraint metric)
COL_EXPMIS <- "mis.exp"          # expected number of missense variants for this gene (proxy for gene size/mutability)

# Where the finished per-gene feature matrix gets written; this is the single
# file that Gene_utility_model.Rmd and Functional_enrichment.Rmd both read in
# as their starting point.
OUT_FILE <- "../../../Data/ML_model_input/gene_heterogeneity_feature_matrix.csv"
```

# 1. Labels

```{r labels, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# monoallelic (dominant) DDG2P universe. Restricted to the two categories used
# throughout the manuscript (Methods, "Gene mechanism classification"):
# monoallelic_autosomal and monoallelic_X_heterozygous. NB: monoallelic_X_HEMIZYGOUS
# is a distinct category (X-linked, hemizygous males) and is NOT included here --
# a naive str_detect(..., "monoallelic") substring match would incorrectly pull
# it in too, since "monoallelic_X_hemizygous" also contains the substring
# "monoallelic". Many DDG2P genes have multiple disease-row entries with
# different allelic requirements (e.g. a gene can cause one disease dominantly
# and a different disease recessively); pull() %>% unique() below correctly
# keeps a gene if ANY of its disease rows matches, which is intended.
## Step 1a: which genes are in scope? (monoallelic/dominant DDG2P genes)
# G2P_DD_2025-04-16.csv is the raw DDG2P export: one row per gene-disease
# association (so the SAME gene can appear on multiple rows, e.g. once for a
# dominant disease and once for an unrelated recessive disease). We clean the
# column names (janitor::clean_names() lower-cases and underscore-separates
# them, e.g. "allelic requirement" -> "allelic_requirement") and then filter
# to just the monoallelic (dominant-acting) disease rows before pulling out
# the distinct gene symbols involved.
g2p <- read_csv("../../../Data/DDG2P/G2P_DD_2025-04-16.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  janitor::clean_names()
MONOALLELIC_CATEGORIES <- c("monoallelic_autosomal", "monoallelic_X_heterozygous")
mono_genes <- g2p %>%
  filter(allelic_requirement %in% MONOALLELIC_CATEGORIES) %>%
  pull(gene_symbol) %>% unique()

## Step 1b: load the two ingredients needed to build the utility LABEL
# `auc`: for each gene, how well does COSMIC missense codon count
# discriminate that gene's pathogenic vs benign ClinVar variants? This
# AUC (and its 95% CI) was already computed by an earlier stage of the
# pipeline (per-gene hold-out benchmarking); here we just read it back in and
# keep only the row for the specific predictor/dataset combination we care
# about (COSMIC missense codon count, ClinVar count-weighted form).
auc <- read_csv("../../../Data/AUC_tables/Gene_group_hold_out_models/Single_feature_AUCs_individual_genes_240426.csv",
                show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(Predictor == "n_COSMIC_codon_count", dataset == "clinvar_long") %>%
  transmute(gene = trimws(gene), auc = AUC_full,
            auc_lower = AUC_full_lower, auc_upper = AUC_full_upper)

# `vc`: for each gene, how many unique pathogenic / benign ClinVar variants
# were available to compute that AUC from? We need this alongside the AUC
# itself because the label definitions below require a minimum variant count
# before trusting the AUC (an AUC computed from only a handful of variants is
# not reliable evidence either way).
vc <- read_csv("../../../Data/AUC_tables/Gene_group_hold_out_models/Variant_counts_per_gene_240426.csv",
               show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(data_set == "clinvar_mutation_data_unique") %>%
  transmute(gene = trimws(gene), n_path_unique = n_path_variants,
            n_benign_unique = n_benign_variants)


# Start from the FULL monoallelic universe (not just benchmarking-eligible
# genes), so grey-zone scoring later extends to genes with too few (or zero)
# ClinVar variants to benchmark individually. auc/vc are left-joined, so these
# genes simply carry NA auc/auc_lower/auc_upper/n_path_unique/n_benign_unique
# -- informative missingness (no benchmarking data available yet), not used as
# a model feature. `eligible` reproduces the original benchmarking-eligibility
# gate and is applied ONLY to the positive/negative label conditions, so the
# positive/negative definitions and counts are unchanged from before; only the
# grey-zone set grows to cover the full monoallelic universe.
# Build the working table: start with ONE row per monoallelic gene (this is
# the full universe we want the final feature matrix to cover), then
# left_join on the AUC and variant-count tables. Because this is a left join
# FROM the full gene list, any gene that isn't in `auc`/`vc` at all (e.g. it
# never had enough ClinVar variants to even attempt an AUC) simply gets NA
# for those columns, rather than being dropped from the table -- this is
# exactly what lets grey-zone scoring extend beyond the benchmarking-eligible
# genes later.
labels <- tibble(gene = mono_genes) %>%
  left_join(auc, by = "gene") %>%
  left_join(vc, by = "gene") %>%
  mutate(
    # `eligible`: does this gene have enough data to trust an AUC-based label
    # at all? Requires a non-missing AUC (i.e. it was possible to compute
    # one) AND at least 10 unique pathogenic and 10 unique benign ClinVar
    # variants. Genes failing this (including all the NA ones from the left
    # join above) cannot be called "positive" or "negative" below, no matter
    # what their AUC looks like.
    eligible = !is.na(auc_lower) & !is.na(n_path_unique) & !is.na(n_benign_unique) &
               n_path_unique >= 10 & n_benign_unique >= 10,
    # The three-way label itself, evaluated top-to-bottom (case_when takes
    # the first matching condition per row):
    #   "positive" -- eligible, AND the AUC's lower 95% CI bound is > 0.70.
    #                 Using the LOWER bound (not the point estimate) is a
    #                 conservative choice: we only call a gene confidently
    #                 high-utility if we're confident even in the worst
    #                 plausible case.
    #   "negative" -- eligible, AND the AUC's upper 95% CI bound is < 0.60,
    #                 AND there are at least 15 (not just 10) unique
    #                 pathogenic variants -- a slightly higher bar than plain
    #                 eligibility, so "negative" genes are genuinely
    #                 well-powered rather than sitting right at the minimum.
    #   "grey"      -- everything else: not eligible at all, OR eligible but
    #                 with an AUC confidence interval that doesn't clearly
    #                 fall on either side of the two thresholds above. These
    #                 genes are scored by the fitted model later but are
    #                 never used to train it.
    label = case_when(
      eligible & auc_lower > 0.70                       ~ "positive",
      eligible & auc_upper < 0.60 & n_path_unique >= 15  ~ "negative",
      TRUE                                               ~ "grey"
    ),
    # Mask the raw AUC/CI to NA for any gene that isn't `eligible`. Without
    # this, a gene can carry a non-NA AUC here purely because it cleared the
    # count-weighted ("clinvar_long") ClinVar-submission-count gate used to
    # build the `auc` table above, even though it has fewer than 10 unique
    # pathogenic and/or 10 unique benign ClinVar variants -- the threshold
    # used everywhere else in the manuscript to decide whether an
    # individual-gene AUC is meaningful. Grey-zone genes should only ever
    # display an AUC that meets that same bar.
    auc       = if_else(eligible, auc,       NA_real_),
    auc_lower = if_else(eligible, auc_lower, NA_real_),
    auc_upper = if_else(eligible, auc_upper, NA_real_)
  ) %>%
  select(-eligible)  # only needed to compute `label`; not a model feature itself

labels %>% count(label) %>% knitr::kable(caption = "Label counts (expect ~40 positive / 84 negative / ~846 grey)")
cat("Total monoallelic genes scored (labelled + grey):", nrow(labels),
    "(expect ~970, matching the manuscript's dominant DD gene universe)\n")
cat("Of these, benchmarking-eligible (>=10 unique path & benign variants):",
    sum(!is.na(labels$auc_lower) & !is.na(labels$n_path_unique) & !is.na(labels$n_benign_unique) &
        labels$n_path_unique >= 10 & labels$n_benign_unique >= 10),
    "(expect ~390)\n")
```

# 2. Non-network features

```{r features-mech, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# --- DD mechanism: two independent binary flags, computed directly from the
# raw DDG2P disease-row entries (`g2p`, loaded above) rather than from a
# precomputed gene-level summary file. A gene can be dd_altfunc, dd_lof, both,
# or neither. Critically, BOTH the allelic-requirement and variant-consequence
# conditions are required on the SAME disease row: a gene with one monoallelic
# disease (e.g. dominant) and a separate biallelic disease (recessive LOF)
# must not have that unrelated recessive-disease mechanism attributed to it as
# a "monoallelic" flag (this is the same disease-row-granularity issue fixed
# for the mono_genes filter above).
#   dd_altfunc = monoallelic disease row(s) with variant_consequence containing
#                "altered gene product structure"
#   dd_lof     = monoallelic disease row(s) with variant_consequence containing
#                "absent gene product" or "decreased gene product level"
dd_mech <- g2p %>%
  filter(allelic_requirement %in% MONOALLELIC_CATEGORIES) %>%
  group_by(gene = gene_symbol) %>%
  summarise(
    dd_altfunc = as.integer(any(str_detect(variant_consequence,
                                           fixed("altered gene product structure")))),
    dd_lof     = as.integer(any(str_detect(variant_consequence, fixed("absent gene product")) |
                                str_detect(variant_consequence, fixed("decreased gene product level")))),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# NB: a handful of genes have NA (not 0/1) here if EVERY monoallelic disease
# row for that gene has a missing variant_consequence; na.rm=TRUE below so the
# printed counts are not silently NA. These NAs are set to 0 (not flagged) in
# the "assemble" step below (replace_na), so the exported feature matrix is
# unaffected -- this is just an honest diagnostic printout.
cat("Monoallelic genes flagged dd_altfunc:", sum(dd_mech$dd_altfunc, na.rm = TRUE),
    "(NA for", sum(is.na(dd_mech$dd_altfunc)), "genes)\n")
cat("Monoallelic genes flagged dd_lof:", sum(dd_mech$dd_lof, na.rm = TRUE),
    "(NA for", sum(is.na(dd_mech$dd_lof)), "genes)\n")
cat("Monoallelic genes flagged BOTH:",
    sum(dd_mech$dd_altfunc & dd_mech$dd_lof, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Monoallelic genes flagged NEITHER (of those with both flags known):",
    sum(!dd_mech$dd_altfunc & !dd_mech$dd_lof, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

# --- Cancer mechanism: two independent binary flags, mirroring dd_altfunc/
# dd_lof above, computed with the SAME logic as the manuscript's own AltFunc/
# LOF gene-group definitions (Scripts/Data_processing_and_annotation/
# Define_cancer_DD_gene_mechanism_sets.Rmd) -- COSMIC CGC only, no OncoKB.
#   cancer_oncogene_missense = ROLE_IN_CANCER contains "oncogene" AND
#                              MUTATION_TYPES contains "Mis" (missense is a
#                              documented mutation type for this gene; this
#                              excludes oncogenes driven only by fusion/
#                              amplification, which would not overlap with
#                              germline missense variants)
#   cancer_tsg               = ROLE_IN_CANCER contains "TSG"
# A gene can be both, neither, or either (independent flags, not mutually
# exclusive categories).
cancer_mech <- read_tsv("../../../Data/Gene_definitions/Cosmic_CancerGeneCensus_v98_GRCh37.tsv.gz",
                        show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(gene = GENE_SYMBOL,
            cancer_oncogene_missense = as.integer(
              str_detect(coalesce(ROLE_IN_CANCER, ""), "oncogene") &
              str_detect(coalesce(MUTATION_TYPES, ""), "Mis")),
            cancer_tsg = as.integer(str_detect(coalesce(ROLE_IN_CANCER, ""), "TSG"))) %>%
  distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE)

cat("Genes flagged cancer_oncogene_missense:", sum(cancer_mech$cancer_oncogene_missense), "\n")
cat("Genes flagged cancer_tsg:", sum(cancer_mech$cancer_tsg), "\n")
cat("Genes flagged BOTH:",
    sum(cancer_mech$cancer_oncogene_missense & cancer_mech$cancer_tsg), "\n")

# --- Hotspot count = number of hotspot residues listed for the gene (a raw
# count, not normalised by protein/CDS length -- NOT a density) ---
hotspots <- read_tsv("../../../Data/Cancer_data/cancerhotspots/hotspots_v2_residues.txt",
                     show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  janitor::clean_names()
# not anchored to "^gene": the source file has a leading UTF-8 BOM before "Gene",
# which janitor::clean_names() sometimes preserves as a stray prefix character.
gcol_h <- names(hotspots)[str_detect(tolower(names(hotspots)), "gene")][1]
stopifnot(!is.na(gcol_h))
hotspot_count <- hotspots %>%
  count(gene = .data[[gcol_h]], name = "hotspot_count")
```

```{r features-constraint, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# --- gnomAD constraint: LOEUF, MOEUF, exp_mis ---
if (!file.exists(GNOMAD_CONSTRAINT_FILE))
  stop("gnomAD constraint file not found: ", GNOMAD_CONSTRAINT_FILE,
       "\nStage the gnomAD v4.1 constraint metrics tsv (see setup chunk).")

constraint_raw <- read_tsv(GNOMAD_CONSTRAINT_FILE, show_col_types = FALSE)
need <- c(COL_GENE, COL_LOEUF, COL_MOEUF, COL_EXPMIS)
miss <- setdiff(need, names(constraint_raw))
if (length(miss) > 0)
  stop("gnomAD constraint file missing expected column(s): ",
       paste(miss, collapse = ", "),
       "\nEdit COL_* in the setup chunk to match your file's headers.")

constraint <- constraint_raw
# keep MANE-select transcript row per gene if that column exists
if (COL_MANE %in% names(constraint)) {
  constraint <- constraint %>%
    filter(tolower(as.character(.data[[COL_MANE]])) %in% c("true", "1", "yes"))
}
constraint <- constraint %>%
  transmute(gene = .data[[COL_GENE]],
            loeuf  = as.numeric(.data[[COL_LOEUF]]),
            moeuf  = as.numeric(.data[[COL_MOEUF]]),
            exp_mis = as.numeric(.data[[COL_EXPMIS]])) %>%
  distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

# 3. Assemble and export

```{r assemble, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
feat <- labels %>%
  left_join(dd_mech,       by = "gene") %>%
  left_join(cancer_mech,   by = "gene") %>%
  left_join(hotspot_count,   by = "gene") %>%
  left_join(constraint,    by = "gene") %>%
  mutate(
    # every gene in `labels` has >=1 monoallelic disease row (by construction),
    # so dd_altfunc/dd_lof are only NA if that row's variant_consequence was
    # empty for every monoallelic disease of that gene; 0 (not flagged) is the
    # correct value here, not a missingness case.
    dd_altfunc               = replace_na(dd_altfunc, 0L),
    dd_lof                   = replace_na(dd_lof, 0L),
    cancer_oncogene_missense = replace_na(cancer_oncogene_missense, 0L),
    cancer_tsg               = replace_na(cancer_tsg, 0L),
    hotspot_count            = replace_na(hotspot_count, 0L)        # no listed hotspots = 0
    # loeuf / moeuf / exp_mis: leave NA here; handle (drop/impute) in the model
    # script and FLAG the missingness explicitly (do NOT silently impute).
  )

# report constraint missingness explicitly rather than silently imputing
cat("Genes missing gnomAD constraint (LOEUF NA):",
    sum(is.na(feat$loeuf)), "of", nrow(feat), "\n")

write_csv(feat, OUT_FILE)
cat("Wrote feature matrix:", OUT_FILE, "\n")
feat %>% count(label, dd_altfunc, dd_lof) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Label x (dd_altfunc, dd_lof) (sanity check)")
feat %>% count(label, cancer_oncogene_missense, cancer_tsg) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Label x (cancer_oncogene_missense, cancer_tsg) (sanity check)")
```
